title: MissionLab scenario, missionlab-plan/1 to missionlab-plan/4
description: A scenario for MissionLab, an unofficial mod toolkit for OPERATOR. missionlab-plan/1, or a file that names no format, holds the scenario at the root. missionlab-plan/2 holds the same body ($defs/missionBody) under "mission" (without its own schema key); it is written only when a zone or hold trigger has a shaped area, so that older versions refuse the file instead of reading the shape as a circle. missionlab-plan/3 is the same envelope, written only when a zone or hold trigger links a named place ("place": the place's id) instead of carrying an area of its own, or when the mission has player goals ("goals", or an extraction with "goals": true); v0.26 reads plan/2 and refuses plan/3, so a link is never read as a circle and goals are never quietly left out. missionlab-plan/4 is the same envelope, written only when a zone or hold trigger waits for another trigger before it watches its area ("after" not 0); the 0.27.0 candidate before it reads plan/3 and would watch such an area from the start, so it refuses plan/4. A mission record written by the Director holds the scenario it played under "plan", and only that is read. The v0.26 keys (sealed, placement, options, director, and scatter, within and fallback on enemies) never force missionlab-plan/2: an older version that ignores them plays the authored content. This schema checks the shape: types, allowed values, where the body sits for each version, that only zone and hold triggers in missionlab-plan/2 or later have an area, that only zone and hold triggers in missionlab-plan/3 or later link a place, never together with an area, that only missionlab-plan/3 or later has goals, and that only missionlab-plan/4 has a zone or hold that waits for another trigger. The plugin (ScenarioFile.cs) and the editor read files strictly by these rules, and also check what a schema cannot say: trigger, place, placement, option, action and goal ids are unique, every link points at a trigger, placement, goal or painted place that exists, a goal or a trigger does not wait for itself, an hvt or a vehicle is never skipped, and every area is a sound shape. Keys that are not listed are ignored.

schema.description: The format, missionlab-plan/1 to /4 ($defs/document). A file with a higher number is refused by this version

mission.description: missionlab-plan/2 to /4 only: the scenario itself, the same keys as a missionlab-plan/1 file without its schema key. A missionlab-plan/1 file with a "mission" is refused

plan.description: A mission record only: the scenario it played, read in place of the record's own keys

id.description: A stable identity that survives renames; the editor makes one (sc- and 10 characters) when a file has none

squad.description: The author's recommended number of players, [fewest, most]

minutes.description: The author's estimate of how long the mission takes; measured times come from run records

mapPrint.description: FNV-1a 64 of the raw bytes of the navmesh file the coordinates were made on, to tell a changed map

places.description: Named places, so that logs and explanations can say where in words; labels only

sealed.description: The Play view hides placements, rolls and future trigger outcomes, so players are not told the mission's secrets

placement.description: Areas scattered enemies may be put in (allow) or must keep out of (empty)

options.description: Choices the host makes before the mission; they use no randomness, so a seed rolls the same dice whatever is picked

budget.description: Points the Game Master starts with

director.description: The Game Master's budget and what it buys; the plugin enforces it for every way of asking

goals.description: missionlab-plan/3 only: player goals (ML-046), each inactive, then active, then succeeded or failed, driven by triggers

scene.description: The game scene it is for; * for any; several separated by commas

navFile.description: The map file it is for, when no scene is named

seed.description: The roll used when the layout was generated

briefing.description: Lines shown one after the other at the start

gameMaster.description: The mission is meant to be run by a Game Master: triggers fired by hand may be part of its way out

skill.description: For every enemy without a skill of its own

nvg.description: Every enemy sees in the dark

after.description: Seconds from the first death to the wave

times.description: Waves per mission; absent for no limit

respawn.description: A shared reinforcement wave: everyone who is dead comes back together

after.description: The extraction stays shut until this trigger has fired

goals.description: The extraction also stays shut until every required goal has succeeded

insertion.description: The insertion every player gets, by its name in the game

weather.description: Weather and time of day, on maps that have them

objectives.description: Where the game's objective items are put

groups.description: How many groups the enemies form; written by the plugin, for people

requestedEnemies.description: How many enemies were asked for when the layout was generated; written by the plugin

document.description: The root rules, for a scenario file or the plan in a mission record: the format decides where the body sits

triggers.description: A link to a named place needs missionlab-plan/3, a zone or hold that waits for another trigger missionlab-plan/4
A zone or hold that waits for another trigger needs missionlab-plan/4

gatedZone.description: A zone (also when "when" is absent) or hold trigger that waits for another trigger before it watches its area: "after" present and not 0. Only missionlab-plan/4 holds one

envelope.description: missionlab-plan/2 to /4: the body under "mission", which names no format of its own. MissionLab reads nothing beside "mission"

plan1.description: missionlab-plan/1, or a file that names no format: the body at the root, without a shaped area, without a link to a place, without a zone or hold that waits for another trigger and without "mission", which only missionlab-plan/2 to /4 read

triggers.description: A shaped area needs missionlab-plan/2, a link to a place missionlab-plan/3, a zone or hold that waits for another trigger missionlab-plan/4

missionBody.description: The scenario itself: at the root in missionlab-plan/1, under "mission" in missionlab-plan/2 to /4. Each key's rule is written once, under the root's properties; tools/schema_check.py checks that this list names the same keys

vec3.description: [x, y, z] in the game's metres

ring.description: A closed outline, either winding, without repeating its first point; it must not cross itself

floor.description: [bottom, top] world height in metres, top above bottom, at most 60 apart

holes.description: Rings inside the outline that are not part of the area; their edges are

parts.description: The area is the union of its parts; at most 2048 points in all

id.description: A whole number from 1, unique among the places

pos.description: Where it is; with an area, only its label

floor.description: [bottom, top] world height in metres for a place given as a point (3 m around pos)

id.description: A whole number from 1, unique among the placements; enemies name it in "within"

mode.description: allow (absent): scattered enemies may be put here; empty: none may be

id.description: Unique among the options; picks are stored by it

pick.description: The choice used when the host picks none, counted from 0

lots.description: Enemies with these lots are left out

respawnTimes.description: Replaces the number of respawn waves; absent: unchanged

skill.description: Replaces the scenario's enemy skill; absent: unchanged

cooldown.description: Seconds before it can be used again

minDistance.description: Metres every player must be away when it fires

unseen.description: Only fires where no player can see

fallback.description: When it cannot fire safely now: wait (absent) and try again for up to 30 s, or cancel

mode.description: How the mission starts: off (absent) decides nothing, preview logs what it would play and fires nothing, on plays the cards by itself; the host can switch it during the session

bands.description: Tried in order; the first whose conditions hold decides how much may be spent and how often

maxEnemies.description: Living enemies the director never pushes past by playing a card; 0 (absent): no cap

rest.description: Seconds without spending after a player goes down; 60 when absent

pressure.description: ML-052, an experiment: an author-bounded pressure director that plays only this block's action cards, through the budget and their own placement rules. Older versions ignore it and play without pacing

from.description: Seconds after the start before the band can apply; 0 when absent

goals.description: Goal ids that must all be active; each must name a goal of the mission

minPlayers.description: Living players the game sees, at least; 0 when absent

spend.description: Most points one decision may spend; the whole budget when absent

every.description: Seconds between decisions while the band applies; 60 when absent

id.description: Unique among the goals; stable, so replays, run records and rehearsals can name it

name.description: Shown to players; cleaned as messages are and cut to 80 characters

required.description: false: optional, never holds the extraction up; absent: required

after.description: Goals that must have succeeded before this one can become active

activate.description: A trigger that must also have fired before it becomes active; absent or 0: none

succeed.description: The trigger whose firing completes it

fail.description: The trigger whose firing fails it; when both have fired by one look, it fails. Absent or 0: none

notify.description: false: players see no "New objective", "Objective complete" or "Objective failed" message for it

then.description: Only zone and hold triggers have an area or link a place

allOf.description: A trigger links a place or has an area of its own, not both

then.description: zone (also when "when" is absent), hold and door triggers need pos
outcome triggers name the trigger they watch and the outcome they wait for

id.description: A whole number from 1, unique in the file

when.description: What it waits for. Absent means zone

pos.description: zone and hold: the middle; door: the door's hinge

area.description: zone and hold, missionlab-plan/2 or later: a shaped place that replaces the circle for who is inside; pos stays the anchor. Never together with place

place.description: zone and hold, missionlab-plan/3 or later: the id of a named place with a painted area, whose shape the trigger uses instead of an area of its own (ML-040). The place must exist and be painted; renaming it keeps the link

facePlayer.description: The enemies it brings face whoever set it off

delay.description: Seconds between its condition and its firing; for time: seconds from the start of the mission

item.description: intel: the item that has to be taken; empty for any

after.description: after: the trigger it waits for; 0 means it is fired by hand. outcome: the trigger whose latest firing it watches (required, must exist). zone and hold, missionlab-plan/4 only: the trigger that has to have fired before it watches its area (0 or absent: from the start; ML-055); the zone's delay or the hold's time count from then

outcome.description: outcome: what the watched trigger's latest firing has to come to. applied: every action was seen to take; failed: an action failed or none of its enemies was made; partial: some of its enemies were made and some not; unconfirmed: the calls went through, nothing could be seen; timeout: no report at all within "within" seconds

within.description: outcome with timeout: seconds the watched firing has to be answered in. Absent means 30

hold.description: hold: seconds a player has to stay inside

count.description: down: how many enemies; 0 for all of them

tag.description: down: only enemies that carry this tag

of.description: all and any: the triggers it waits for

chance.description: Percent: on other missions the trigger sits out

warn.description: Tell the players how long is left: at the start of the wait, at five minutes, one minute and ten seconds

everyone.description: zone and hold: every living player has to be inside

repeat.description: Seconds after which it may fire again; 0 means once

times.description: With repeat: how often it fires in all; 0 for no limit

rally.description: Metres: enemies this close walk to the trigger's place when it fires

hunt.description: The enemies it brings walk to the nearest player

respawn.description: Dead players come back when it fires

message.description: Shown on every screen; {enemies}, {players} and {time} are filled in. At most 120 characters

red.description: The message is a red warning

doors.description: Doors it locks, unlocks, opens or closes

role.description: Guard, Wander, Patrol, and the special kinds of the game

fixed.description: A sentry that does not move

type.description: The game's enemy type; empty for the map's usual

patrol.description: The stops of a patrol route

trigger.description: The trigger that brings this enemy; 0 or absent: there from the start

hvt.description: The target person, in missions that have one

lot.description: Enemies with the same lot share one roll

option.description: Which option of the set this enemy belongs to

minPlayers.description: Only there with at least this many players

tag.description: A name of your choosing, for 'tagged enemies down' triggers

scatter.description: Metres: placed at random this far from pos at most when the mission starts, on the same floor

within.description: The allow placement the scattered position must lie in

fallback.description: When no scattered position passes: stay at pos (absent), or leave the enemy out; never skip for an hvt or a vehicle

name.description: The door's name in the game, for people; the door is found by pos

locked.description: true: locked, false: unlocked, absent: as the game decides

open.description: true: stands open (and is unlocked), false: closed; in a trigger: what the trigger does to it

chance.description: Percent, 1 to 100: the door setting is only used on that share of missions

name.description: The game's name of the thing, such as AKM

trigger.description: Placed when this trigger fires; 0 or absent: from the start
